Subject: Tombstone retention & backup exclusion - DPA question

Hi Karthik,

Quick follow to the DPA review — Greenfield's security team raised two narrow asks around backups and 'tombstone' artifacts that I want to surface before we go to signature:

1) Backup/DR carve-out: They want to ensure that for disaster recovery purposes Redwood may retain encrypted backup snapshots for a limited period (to be used only for restore) but that these backups do not constitute continued processing for product analytics or training. They asked for a short clause saying backups are only used for restore and must be overwritten within X days after restore, and that customer PII is not purposefully processed in backups beyond what's necessary.

2) Tombstone / soft-delete handling: Greenfield engineers retain tombstones in their systems for operational reasons. They want confirmation of the deletion workflow — specifically that when objects are deleted in production, Redwood will (a) remove active copies within 30 days, (b) purge tombstones from hot caches within 7 days, and (c) document backup retention windows so they can provide that in their internal audit.

Can you confirm whether Redwood accepts a narrowly scoped backup/DR carve-out and the deletion timeline above (30/7)? If not, please propose Redwood's standard language and timing.

Samir (cc'd) is the security lead and will review any redlines. Also: do you require an executed SOW or amendment before these carve-outs are accepted?

Thanks — Alicia

Thanks Karthik — reviewing now, drafting redline. Summary of Redwood's position (for Greenfield):

1) Backup/DR snapshots (accepted carve-out):
- Purpose limitation: Backups retained solely for disaster recovery and restore operations. Backups will not be used for model training, analytics, or product improvement unless explicit, separate consent is obtained.
- Retention: Encrypted backups will be retained in object storage for a maximum of 60 days unless required by law to retain longer; however, for the purpose of restores we will commit to overwriting backup snapshots within 30 days after a restore completion (i.e., 30-day overwrite window post-restore).
- Access controls: Access to backup snapshots is limited to the incident response/DR team and protected by role-based access and audit logging.

2) Tombstone / soft-delete handling:
- Active data deletion: Redwood will remove active production copies of customer data within 30 days of deletion request or customer-initiated delete action.
- Hot cache/tombstone purge: For operational caches where tombstones are maintained, Redwood will purge tombstones from hot caches within 7 days; tombstones may persist longer in cold backups subject to the backup retention above.
- Proof of deletion: Upon reasonable request, Redwood will provide a deletion attestation describing the deletion workflow and timestamps; full forensic proof (bit-level) will require a legal process and may be scoped in a SOC/forensic request.

3) Scope and exceptions:
- The carve-out explicitly excludes processing for diagnostics, analytics, or training.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will ensure subprocessors handling backups adhere to the same constraints in their DPA terms and will list relevant subprocessors on the standard subprocessor page.

I attach a short redline for the DPA (Greenfield_DPA_redline_v3.docx) with the above language inserted into the retention and backups section. I also recommend adding a brief sentence in the termination and disaster recovery section clarifying the overwrite commitment post-restore.

On SOW: not necessary for the DPA language change — standard DPA amendment (electronic signature) suffices. Marissa, can sales finalize the DocuSign and confirm the signing owner?

Neha
